Maintenance Report — MNT-0092-004

Asset: WELL-0092 (SW-24 Well 092, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 20 May 2023 08:00 · Finished: 14 Jun 2023 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 603 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0092-0028 on 2023-05-18 Report written: 14 Jun 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0092-0028 showed the wellhead at 36.5 °C with the air at 33.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 23 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 8 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

  • Send the old pump for teardown.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0092-006

Asset: WELL-0092 (SW-24 Well 092, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 23 Jun 2023 08:00 · Finished: 05 Jul 2023 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 282 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0092-0033 on 2023-06-22 Report written: 05 Jul 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw a thin film of oil on the wellhead. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0092-0033 showed the wellhead at 35.4 °C with the air at 35.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 10 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Normal packing wear.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 8 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0092-007

Asset: WELL-0092 (SW-24 Well 092, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 14 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 14 Jul 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0092-0036 on 2023-07-13 Report written: 15 Jul 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0092-0036 at 15:15 on 2023-07-13 found crude oil on the pad: about 5.6% of the pad area, estimated 1.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 279 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 223 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.0 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0092-007 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.37% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Parts and cost

Flange gasket and bolts529
Absorbents and berms1,058
Soil hauling and disposal1,941
Labour (company crew and contractor)3,103
Total6,631

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 4 ppm
WS-05MetTested at 1.25 × maximum operating pressure, held 4 hours
WS-06MetOily waste manifested to an approved site
WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)
SR-02MetContained about 1.5 hours after discovery (limit 4 hours)
SR-04MetSpill recorded with volume and area (moderate class)
HSE noticeMetHSE notified 15 hours after discovery (company limit 72 hours for moderate spills)

Notes and recommendations

  • Inspect the remaining joints on this flowline.
  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).
